decision.why: THE RULE ALREADY SAYS WHAT IT DETECTS, AND IT IS NOT A BRACE. key.template_detection.rule at v1.11 defines the object as 'the producer's own runtime substitution field'; the brace was the EVIDENCE its authors had for that field in the 15 round-7 rows, never the definition. 'silver/%s/' is that object in a different syntax -- in both producers it is the constant SILVER_PREFIX_FMT (infra/aws/lambda/bd-pipeline/bd-49f-freshness-probe/lambda_function.py:69, infra/aws/lambda/cot-pipeline/bd-cot-freshness-probe/lambda_function.py:67), a format string by its own name. HOLD would have to write into the standard that this row is a NAME, which its own producer says it is not, and would leave the census grading it into the canonical '{source}/{scope}/silver/%s/' -- a canonical that still carries an unfilled substitution field. THE POPULATION DECIDES THE SIZE, NOT THE DIRECTION, AND IT CUTS TOWARD WIDEN: inside the graded corpus the %-style class is 2 of 3254 census rows (one distinct value), so widening moves at most those 2 rows when a later round re-grades; but the unscoped read finds 44 tier-prefixed %-style key literals in 33 tracked .py files, 11 of them first-party producers (etf-ownership, fees-runner, bronze ingest, gold holdings, coverage, month-end render, both freshness probes), 42 of which the census never admitted. %-style is a LIVE key-format convention of this estate, not a one-off: a brace-only rule would grade every one of them as a name the moment the census extractor admits it. THE COST OF WIDEN IS AMBIGUITY, AND IT IS BOUNDED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AWAY: '%' also introduces a URL-encoded byte, a literal percent, strftime, and printf forms no key uses. The schema admits exactly four forms (%s; %d not before a hex digit; %(name)s|%(name)d; %0Nd, N 1-99) and names what stays out; measured, that bound selects 44 of 44 real tier-prefixed %-literals and 2 of 2 census %-rows, and leaves ORDINARY 3237 of 3237 ordinary census rows, 20 of 20 genuine URL-encoded repo literals, and 16 of 16 look-alike exemplars -- where the broad printf predicate the population census itself used mis-reads real URL bytes ('a%20secret' as a width-20 %s, '%5ESPX' as a width-5 %E). NO GRADE MOVES THIS ROUND: no code reads key.template_detection, and the re-grade is a later round's cut.
